text:
Aleksander Barkov played his first game back from injury on Wednesday, a 5-3 win over Ottawa, and the Panthers' own video caught the moment under the title "You made it special for me." Brad Marchand was set to come back alongside him. For a team that is 3-1-1 in its last five and sits at 71% to make the playoffs by our numbers, getting two of its biggest pieces back in the same week changes the shape of the lineup. Brady Tkachuk is playing a third-line role, about 15:51 a night, and his shots over the last ten games have been more dangerous than 98% of depth forwards'. He is our sleeper tonight at 31% to score.

Washington just snapped an 0-5-0 skid by running the Flyers 7-3, but the problem behind that run hasn't gone anywhere. Logan Thompson is at .877 and 2.8 goals worse than expected this season, and he was pulled in Buffalo after two goals in 25 seconds. The Capitals have taken 54% of the expected goals at five on five (the share of quality chances), and their goaltending has allowed 10.2 more goals than the shots deserved. That gap is most of why they're at 42% for the playoffs instead of comfortably in.

There's also the Alex Ovechkin story, which will follow every Capitals game this season, billed as his final one. The franchise held a ceremony for his assist record, and he hasn't scored in 17 games despite 4.5 expected goals. The scoring has come from elsewhere: Alex Tuch has goals in four straight, and Ryan Leonard has a six-game point streak, the longest of his career.

Jacob Markstrom has been the steadier goalie lately, 3.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Our numbers expect 3.63 goals for Washington and 3.23 for Florida. Sam Bennett is one goal from 200, Seth Jones one point from 500.
headline: Barkov is back, and Washington needs a save
